title: PUCT to Host First Public Workshop on Advanced Nuclear Reactors

  Public Utility Commission of Texas to Host First Public Workshop on Advanced
                                 Nuclear Reactors


Austin, Texas – The Public Utility Commission of Texas’ (PUCT) newly-formed Texas Advanced
Nuclear Reactor Working Group will host its first public workshop on Thursday, Sept. 28 at 2 p.m.
CT. The workshop will take place at the PUCT in the Commissioners’ Hearing Room at 1701 N.
Congress Ave. Austin, Texas 78701 (7th Floor) and will be livestreamed on the PUCT’s website.

Governor Greg Abbott directed the PUCT to form the Texas Advanced Nuclear Reactor Working
Group in a letter on Aug. 16 and designated Commissioner Jimmy Glotfelty to lead the initiative.
The working group will study and plan for the use of advanced nuclear reactors in Texas and
submit a formal report to Governor Abbott outlining how the state can become a national leader
in advanced nuclear energy.

“I thank Governor Abbott for his leadership and direction on this important issue,” Commissioner
Glotfelty said. “Providing safe, reliable, and affordable energy for a growing number of Texans will
require harnessing every available source of dispatchable power. Nuclear energy is reliable,
technologically advanced, and has great potential to help Texas meet its future power needs. I
look forward to bringing industry, state and federal agencies, and Texas’ leading research
universities to the table to chart a path forward.”

Governor Abbott directed the working group to “understand the state’s role in deploying and
using advanced nuclear reactors; consider all potential financial incentives available, determine
nuclear-specific changes needed in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) market;
identify any federal or state regulatory impediments to development; and identify how the state
can streamline and accelerate permitting for the building of advanced nuclear reactors in Texas.”
The working group must also study and evaluate advances in nuclear reactor safety and
technology.

The Sept. 28 workshop will provide an opportunity to discuss the working group’s organizational
structure and outline a plan for carrying out the Governor’s directives. Interested parties and
stakeholders are invited to share their thoughts on the working group’s structure, process, and
timeline.

Documents related to the Texas Advanced Nuclear Reactor Working Group’s ongoing work,
 including a recent memo on participation from Commissioner Glotfelty and an announcement for
the upcoming public workshop, will be filed under PUCT Project #55421. Public comments and
questions may also be filed in the project. Instructions for filing a document with the PUCT are
available here.


About the Public Utility Commission
Our mission is to serve Texans by regulating the state’s electric, telecommunication, and water
and sewer utilities, implementing respective legislation, and offering assistance in resolving
consumer complaints. Since its founding in 1975, the Commission has a long and proud history of
service to Texas, protecting consumers, fostering competition, and promoting high quality
infrastructure. To learn more, please visit https://www.puc.texas.gov.
